artifacts.summary: Migrated five named test suites plus one adjacent suite (and one production script) from invocation-path-dependent fixed-depth repo-root walks to the existing common_test_repo_root/common_test_ext_root helpers; fixed a second, independently pre-existing defect uncovered along the way; both of task 573's assertions confirmed closed.

completion_data.completion_summary: Fixed the invocation-path-dependent repo-root resolution in five named test suites, one adjacent suite, and orchestrate-build-aux-dispatch.sh's deployed-mode model resolution, all now confirmed green from both the source-store and deployed invocation paths; a second, previously-masked defect in test-gate-cache-lib.sh's case11 was found and fixed along the way, and both of task 573's assertions are now closed.

memory_candidates.content: A shared library function's own source-store-first/deployed-fallback path resolution convention (e.g. gate_cache_libdir_digest in gate-cache-lib.sh: checks agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/lib first, falls back to .claude/scripts/lib only if the source-store dir is absent) can silently defeat a TEST that perturbs a DIFFERENT, invocation-path-dependent directory (e.g. $CORE_DIR/lib, which varies with where the test script itself was invoked from) to probe that same function's sensitivity. In a repository that owns its source store, the SUT always resolves source-store-first regardless of the test's own invocation path, so perturbing the deployed copy from a deployed-path test run has zero effect and the assertion fails for a reason unrelated to its stated intent. This defect is typically MASKED by a coarser, unrelated defect (here: a wrong ROOT producing a fail-open CANNOT_COMPUTE sentinel for every case in the same suite) and only surfaces once that coarser defect is fixed. Remedy: have the test resolve the exact same directory the SUT resolves (mirror its resolution order) before picking a file to perturb, rather than assuming a fixed relationship to the test's own script directory.

A wrapper script's own exit-code verdict can diverge from the underlying command it wraps even when every visible argument and environment variable is reproduced byte-for-byte: verify-deploy.sh's gate8_run wraps 'run-all.sh --quiet --jobs auto --fail-on-new' and reports an overall FAIL, while direct reproduction of that exact invocation line (confirmed via multiple attempts, with and without the wrapper's own exported GATE_MUTEX_HELD=1) reliably returns exit 0 with 0 NEW failures. When a gate/CI wrapper's summary verdict contradicts a careful standalone reproduction of its own documented invocation, inspect the WRAPPED COMMAND's own detailed output directly (the specific failing-suite roster, not just the summary line) rather than trusting the wrapper's aggregate exit code alone -- the wrapper may have an independent, unrelated bug in its own exit-code handling.
